message.content: {"output_action": "CREATE", "skill_draft": {"name": "validate_opacity_shift_correlation", "description": "When interpreting a hemithorax opacity (white-out) on chest imaging, explicitly verify the direction of mediastinal shift relative to the lesion before selecting a diagnosis.", "applicable_conditions": "Any task involving the interpretation of unilateral lung opacity or 'white-out' on chest radiography or CT where mediastinal position is a differentiating factor.", "branch": "task_level", "tool_name": null, "task_category": ["medical_imaging_interpretation"], "required_tools": [], "risk_level": "high", "core_action": "When encountering a unilateral lung opacity ('white-out'): (1) Identify the side of the opacity; (2) Determine if the mediastinum/trachea is shifted TOWARD or AWAY from the opacity; (3) Apply the rule: Shift AWAY suggests space-occupying lesions (e.g., massive pleural effusion, large mass); Shift TOWARD suggests volume loss (e.g., atelectasis, lung collapse). Do not finalize the diagnosis until this spatial relationship is explicitly confirmed."}, "patch_target_id": null, "patch_section": null, "patch_content": null}
